title: Delineating Oxidation Aspects of an Additively Manufactured Nanoprecipitation-Strengthened Al<sub>0.2</sub>Co<sub>1.5</sub>CrFeNi<sub>1.5</sub>Ti<sub>0.3</sub> High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: Additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy produced (likely by laser powder‐bed fusion) with a nanoscale precipitation-strengthened matrix
recollection.intervention: High-temperature oxidation tests (isothermal and/or cyclic up to ~1000–1100 °C) followed by characterization with TGA, XRD, SEM/TEM, EDS, and possibly atom-probe tomography
recollection.structure: A duplex oxide scale consisting mainly of continuous external Al2O3 (with some Cr2O3/TiO2 or spinel) over a fine-grained FCC matrix containing coherent L12 nano-precipitates (e.g., Ni3(Al,Ti))
recollection.mechanism: Selective outward diffusion of Al (assisted by Cr) forms a slow-growing protective alumina layer; nano-precipitates and AM-refined grains provide fast diffusion paths that accelerate initial scale development but later block cation transport, stabilizing the scale
recollection.results: Guessed values: parabolic oxidation rate constant kp ≈ 1–3 × 10⁻¹² g² cm⁻⁴ s⁻¹ at 1000 °C; total mass gain after 100 h at 1000 °C ~0.1 mg cm⁻²—about 30 % lower than a conventionally cast counterpart; cyclic oxidation shows <5 % spallation after 100 cycles between room temperature and 1000 °C

score.note: The recollection identifies high-temperature oxidation testing and partially recalls an FCC matrix with L12 nanoprecipitates and a multilayer oxide, but it misses the key as-printed versus 750°C/50 h aged comparison and the L21 precipitates. It incorrectly identifies alumina as the continuous protective scale; the actual barrier was Cr-rich, primarily Cr2O3. The proposed Al-diffusion mechanism is therefore wrong, and all quantitative values are guessed and inconsistent with the reported exponents and activation energies.
